content:
If you've recently purchased a new Mac, such as the recently released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you may also want to add a new external display.

Below are my recommendations, covering multiple product categories, price ranges, and other factors.

Best External Displays for Mac

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best displays on the market, Apple's Studio Display is absolutely indispensable to mention. Although it is on the pricey side, it comes equipped with a 27-inch 5K display, and the design is full of Apple's aesthetic appeal.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Colour Support: Wide colour gamut (P3), supporting 1 billion colours
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • True Tone Technology: Automatically adjusts the display's colour temperature to match ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in several configurations with different prices, which I have listed below. If you love the iMac experience but are using a Mac, then the Apple Studio Display is the best choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR, launched earlier this year, offers several significant advantages over the standard Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness, up to 2,000 nits HDR peak brightness
  • Colour Support: P3 and Adobe RGB wide colour gamut, supporting 1 billion colours
  • Refresh Rate: 120Hz, with Adaptive Sync support
  • Host Charging: Up to 140W

Of course, these advantages also make it more expensive than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor features a 4K OLED panel, making it a very appealing choice for Mac users. My 9to5Toys colleague Justin Kahn switched to this monitor and said that "over the past few months using it with my Mac mini has been a real pleasure."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh Rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2× USB-A
  • Built-in Camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR Support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although it doesn't offer the sharp 5K or 6K resolution like some other options on the list, you'll enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks, better colour reproduction, and superior contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor now:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K is LG's high-end evolution in the display market. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels, and plenty of ports. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Colour Support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colours (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • True Tone Technology: None; supports auto-brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast Ratio: 2,000:1

Where to buy the LG UltraFine 6K

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin got hands-on time with this display, and it immediately caught my eye. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K display offers the same 5K resolution (5120×2880), 27-inch size similar to the Studio Display, but at half the price.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Colour Support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB, and 95% Adobe RGB, supporting 1.07 billion colours (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz, with Adaptive-Sync support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Light Adjustment: Ambient light and backlight sensors automatically adjust brightness and colour temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C supporting DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

For all the details, check out Jeff's full review. If you're on the hunt for a 5K display to pair with your Mac, the Asus ProArt is virtually an unbeatable choice.

Where to buy the Asus ProArt 5K Display:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you want a larger size and higher resolution, Asus has you covered. The new Asus ProArt 6K display (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch display with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "absurdly good value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Colour Support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colours (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz, with Adaptive-Sync support (48–60Hz)
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub connectivity, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

The biggest selling point of the ASUS ProArt 6K display may be its price. It's significantly cheaper than some of the most popular 4K and 5K displays on the market.

Where to buy the ASUS ProArt 6K Display:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another appealing option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits
  • Colour Support: 99% sRGB, supporting 1.07 billion colours; HDR10
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Light Adjustment: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness according to ambient lighting
  • Ports: One USB-C port with 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Where to buy the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Display

This may be my current favourite choice. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K display comes packed with Mac-friendly features, and the standout is of course the sharp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: Typical and peak 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Colour Support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709, and 98% P3, supporting 1.07 billion colours
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller with customisable controls

Where to buy the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K Display:

Read our full review: The BenQ 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 Designer Monitor is a worthy contender against the Apple Studio Display

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Display

If you're looking for a 32-inch display for your new Mac but want to keep it under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options. Its biggest drawback, however, is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. That said, it comes with a rich selection of ports, and the 32-inch panel is priced under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Colour Support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colours
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Light Adjustment: No automatic ambient light colour temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Where to buy the BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Display:

Read our full review: Should 32-inch 4K Mac displays really be ruled out?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultra-Wide Display

If you want to pair an ultra-wide display with your Mac, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display. It also features a rich port selection, matte screen, and more.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2,500R curvature
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Colour Support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB, and 100% Rec.709, supporting 1.07 billion colours
  • Refresh Rate: Up to 120Hz, with VRR support
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Light Adjustment: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and colour temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host Charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Where to buy the Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultra-Wide Display:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

For those looking to enter the ultra-wide display market at a more affordable price point, the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC is an option, and it's currently available at nearly half price. Although it doesn't have everything that some other options offer, you still get a 34-inch ultra-wide curved display and a rich port selection, including a Thunderbolt 4 port with power delivery support.

  • Display: 34-inch ultra-wide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1,000R curvature for an immersive viewing experience
  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (delivering up to 90W of power), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port, and one 3.5mm headphone jack

Where to buy the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC:

Wrap-up

Above are just some of the best external display options to pair with your new Mac. They all offer excellent macOS integration, a rich selection of connectivity options, and unique sizes and designs.

Have you recently bought a new Mac? Which display are you using to pair with it? Feel free to share in the comments section.
